Code read: HouseEnv.finish loops on the world clock (`while time_s < end - 1e-6`, engine.py:1416). _substep stores round(time_s + dt, 3) (engine.py:1190), so a remaining settle under 0.5 ms advances nothing. _advance's own loop ends on `remaining` and so terminates, but finish re-enters it forever. The look-ahead calls _idle_frame once and cannot hang. The only checks on the input are range checks: finish (0..600) and spec.check_structure (spec.py:477-480, `0 <= value <= SETTLE_MAX_S`). The defect is real: P7 says every run has a cap, and the gate would hang without output. Severity corrected to low because the trigger is contrived. Every caller (verify.reference_run / wrong_run / _confirm_sample, perceive.py:345, the replay at engine.py:1882) passes the task's own settle_s or the default 60. No authored spec sets a spec-level settle_s (the settle_s hits in tools_vehicles__examples.json are skill arguments). Only a hand-written sub-millisecond fraction (e.g. 30.0004) reaches the loop. The fix is trivial and belongs in engine.py: stop when a frame advanced less than 1 ms, or round `end` to the clock grid. WP8 may also reject off-grid values.
